summary: Surge-driven pin resilience exhaustion causes progressive fallback and degraded outputs
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported a cascade of degraded responses and elevated 5xxs after a short traffic spike. The tenant had a pinned model version for a subset of sessions (rw-instruct-v1). During the spike the routing plane performed several fallbacks; instead of a single immediate failover, a progressive sequence of alternate model choices occurred and several sessions lost pin affinity mid-request.

Impact:
- ~18% of requests for the tenant saw content-quality regressions (responses truncated or hallucinating facts) for a 9-minute window.
- Observed transient 502/503 errors for streaming connections and sporadic 429s as routing retried.
- Customer-facing application showed degraded UX and a support page was posted.

Environment:
- Production, us-west cluster. Dedicated capacity reservation for Neutrino Labs (dedicated pool id: dp-77).
- Maintenance window for one GPU node group had been scheduled and partially executed earlier that morning (node drain started at 09:07 UTC).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer traffic spike at 09:12 UTC (burst to ~3x baseline for ~6 minutes).
2) Autoscaler responded by attempting to allocate replacement workers; spot reclaim and maintenance drain reduced available capacity in the pinned pool.
3) Routing attempted to preserve model pins using pin-resilience policy (max_retries=3, fallback_order configured).
4) Prefix/KV cache entries for some sessions expired due to memory pressure; affinity tokens TTLs were refreshed inconsistently across edge nodes.
5) Some requests hit an instance that had already been drained and returned early fallback decisions, which triggered a chain of re-routing through canary variants and older model versions.
6) Several sessions lost their pinned affinity mid-stream and received responses from a smaller, older model (gptx-13b) with different tokenization/templating, producing degraded outputs.

Logs & Observables (key snippets):
- Routing logs: "pin-resilience: retries_exhausted tenant=neutrino-p123 attempts=3" repeated for multiple session-ids.
- Edge proxy: "stream: upstream-reset after fallback" aligned with 09:15:21–09:17:30 UTC.
- Autoscaler: "scale_out request queued: lack_of_quota in dp-77" then "node_drain in progress: group nodegroup-3".
- Prefix cache evictions: high evict rate in us-west prefix-cache (~98 evictions/min at 09:14).
- Traces: trace ids showing stepwise fallbacks across three different model endpoints within a single logical request.

Initial hypothesis:
- Capacity contraction (node drain + spot evictions) concurrent with a traffic surge caused pin-resilience retries to exhaust. When retries exhausted, the routing plane applied fallback_order sequentially rather than atomic rebind, causing mid-request multi-hop re-routing and pin-affinity loss. Prefix cache pressure and non-atomic token refresh amplified the effect.

Investigation notes:
- SRE reproduced approximate scenario in staging by simulating node drain + synthetic burst; observed similar progressive fallback behavior when pin-resilience retry limit hit while prefix-cache eviction rate high.
- Route-manager code path: found a window where a session's affinity token is checked, then reclaimed by another controller thread before the rebind completes; this allowed partial fallback decisions to be applied. Race condition appears in route-manager v2.7.2 when binder locks are contended.
- Autoscaler rate-limiting combined with dedicated pool quota checks delayed replacement workers for ~90s in the incident window.
- Canary weight recalculation logic applied updates per-edge node with eventual consistency; some edges had stale weight leading them to choose older model variants while others chose canary.

Customer impact timeline (UTC):
- 09:12:00: burst begins.
- 09:14:20: prefix-cache eviction spike observed.
- 09:15:00–09:24:00: progressive fallbacks and quality regressions recorded.
- 09:25:30: autoscaler succeeded in provisioning replacement; pool capacity restored.
- 09:28:00: prefix cache recovered; pins stabilized; incident largely subsided.

Comments:
comments: Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-10T10:02Z: Customer opened ticket, included session ids, sample payloads, and timestamps. Notified on-call SRE and assigned to Diego.
SRE (Diego Alvarez) 2026-03-10T10:25Z: Began correlation with autoscaler and routing logs, reproducing in staging; suspect race in route-manager binder under high eviction pressure.
Customer (K. Rao, Neutrino Labs) 2026-03-10T11:05Z: Confirmed we saw degraded answers and several aborted streams. Customer requires assurance on pin stability during maintenance windows.
SRE (Diego Alvarez) 2026-03-11T08:40Z: Hotfix PR created to add stronger binder locking + early capacity check to avoid fallbacks when pinned pool has queued replacements (see PRs linked).

Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-12T09:10Z: Communicated workaround to customer: increase pin-resilience.retry_limit to 6 and enable conservative fallback_order for the tenant until patch is deployed. Customer accepted temporary config change.
Engineering (Lina Park) 2026-03-12T14:00Z: Added postmortem task to ensure prefix-cache eviction alarms surface earlier and to add edge-coordinated canary weight sync to avoid inconsistent choices.
investigation: Repro in staging confirmed race between binder token refresh and node drain flow. Root cause is non-atomic pin rebind logic under eviction pressure plus delayed autoscaler replacement. Also observed canary weight staleness across edges leading to mixed model decisions. Priority: fix binder atomicity, improve autoscaler fast-path for reserved pools, and add early eviction alerts.
resolution: Temporary: increased tenant pin-resilience.retry_limit to 6 and switched tenant fallback policy to prefer stable downgrade path rather than canary hops. Long-term: merged PR to make binder rebind atomic (serving-runtime + route-manager) and added pre-drain capacity checks in autoscaler (PRs linked). Deployed patch to us-west at 2026-03-12T03:20Z; no further regressions observed in follow-up load tests. Follow-ups: add automated chaos test combining drain + burst, and lower prefix-cache eviction threshold alarms.
next_steps: ENG-1: Ship atomic binder rebind to all regions (tracking PR merged, rollout in progress)
OPS-2: Add pre-drain capacity verification to scheduled maintenance runbook
SRE-3: Create chaos test for combined drain + burst scenarios and add to CI
PM-4: Notify customer of permanent mitigations and schedule a postmortem sync
